blocks.content:
The Watchers page is under **AI** in the main menu. Create a watcher by describing the service, system, or failure mode to monitor. Keep the scope narrow: one service, namespace, cluster, or failure mode. Include context Assistant can't infer from telemetry, for example whether short error spikes during deploys are expected.

You don't need to define what a problem looks like. Calibration works out what normal looks like from your telemetry.
To open the create form, complete the following steps:

blocks.hint: If the page isn't available, confirm Assistant is enabled and that you have Watchers read permission. Watchers isn't available in self-managed Grafana. In the main menu, **Watchers** is under **AI**.

blocks.content:
Click **New watcher**.

You need `grafana-assistant-app.watcher-agents:create` to create a watcher.

You're on the **New watcher** form.

Before you fill it in, pick one thing to watch that has live data. If you're not sure what has data, open **Explore** in a new browser tab, choose a Prometheus data source, switch the query editor to **Code**, and run `count by (job) (up)`. Each job in the results is sending metrics now, and you can watch any of them.
To fill in the form and create the watcher, complete the following steps:

blocks.title: Fill in and create the watcher

blocks.content:
In **Name**, enter the service or check you want to watch.

Pick something your data sources have telemetry for. You'll look this name up later in the Watchers list.

In **Give the watcher context**, describe what to watch and anything it can't learn from telemetry, such as expected rollout behavior, known noise, or acceptable tolerances.

For example: "Watch the payments API in production. Short error spikes during deploys are expected, but errors should recover within a few minutes."

If you picked a job in **Explore**, you can write: "Watch the Prometheus job integrations/node_exporter. Raise concern if any host goes down or stops reporting." Replace the job name with yours.
blocks.hint: Name the same service here as in **Name**. Calibration fails if your data sources have no telemetry for what you describe.

blocks.content:
In **Datasources**, pick at least one data source, for example Prometheus or Loki, that has telemetry for the service you're watching.

If you used **Explore**, pick only the data source you queried there.
blocks.hint: Only pick data sources that return data. A data source with no data can make calibration fail.

blocks.content:
Leave **Repeats** at **Every 10 minutes**.

You can choose any interval from every 5 minutes to every 3 hours.
blocks.hint: Skip if you already changed the interval.

blocks.content:
Leave **Sensitivity** at **Balanced**.

Change it only if you know the watcher should be more or less sensitive.
blocks.hint: Skip if you already changed sensitivity.

blocks.content:
Leave the rest of the form as it is, then click **Create watcher**.

For this intro, you don't need **Labels**, **Stop automatically**, the **Notifications** settings, or **Launch on a critical assessment**. You can configure notifications later from the watcher's page.
blocks.hint: **Create watcher** stays disabled until **Name**, **Give the watcher context**, and **Datasources** are filled.

blocks.content: You created a watcher with a name, context, data sources, cadence, and sensitivity. Grafana opened its **Calibration** tab, and calibration is now running in the background. In the next milestone, you'll follow calibration and review the checks it saves.
